title: Governance, Compliance and Medical Device Security
answer: Enablement audits, local models for patient data, device clearance, bias in triage and connected device security.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit in Healthcare
children.blurb: The AI Enablement Audit in Healthcare is a structured review of how a care organisation selects, deploys and monitors artificial intelligence tools that touch patient care, clinical operations or billing.

children.name: Local Models for Patient Data
children.blurb: Local models for patient data are AI systems that run on hardware inside a hospital, clinic or research site rather than sending records to an external service.

children.name: Software as a Medical Device
children.blurb: Software as a Medical Device covers any software that a manufacturer intends to be used for a medical purpose, whether it runs on dedicated hardware, a general purpose computer, a phone or in the cloud.

children.name: Bias in Clinical Triage
children.blurb: Bias in clinical triage covers the ways an automated system that sorts, scores or prioritises patients can produce systematically different outcomes for different groups.

children.name: Security of Connected Medical Devices
children.blurb: Connected medical devices are instruments that hold a network link, whether that is an infusion pump on a hospital wireless LAN, a pacemaker with a bedside monitor, or a home glucose reader that uploads to a phone.

sections.body: Governance, compliance and medical device security is the work of making clinical AI answerable to the same standards as any other tool used on patients. In practice this means auditing how a model was enabled and validated, deciding where patient data is allowed to live, and proving to regulators that software making a clinical claim is safe and effective. Hospitals now run enablement audits before deployment, keep some models on local infrastructure so records never leave the building, and treat triage scoring tools as candidates for device clearance. Security teams watch connected pumps, monitors and imaging systems because a compromised device is a patient safety event, not just an IT incident. The field sits where data protection law, medical device regulation and clinical risk management meet.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are settled. Software as a medical device has an established regulatory path in major markets, and the general principle that patient data should stay under the provider's control is widely accepted, which is why local and on premises models have moved from experiment to routine option. Other parts are not settled. Bias in clinical triage is measurable but there is no single agreed threshold for when a model is fair enough to deploy, and audit methods vary between institutions. Connected device security remains difficult because equipment lifetimes run for a decade or more while patching cycles are slow and legacy protocols persist. The honest limit is that compliance evidence shows a process was followed, not that a model is clinically correct, and no audit removes the need for clinical oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the path a clinical AI system takes from procurement to ongoing operation. The AI Enablement Audit in Healthcare covers the review that happens before deployment, asking what the model was trained on and who signed off. Local Models for Patient Data takes up the infrastructure choice that keeps records inside the provider's boundary. Software as a Medical Device explains when a tool crosses into regulated territory and what clearance then requires. Bias in Clinical Triage examines how scoring tools can disadvantage groups and how that is detected. Security of Connected Medical Devices closes the loop on the hardware these systems touch. A reader new to the area should start with the audit page, while those already deploying should go to the triage bias and device security pages for the operational risks.
